Brouwer on trace-one positive matrices gives a positive-definite moment eigenmatrix; log-determinant strict concavity makes the eigenvalue greater than one for a nondegenerate law; the adjoint gives the exact energy identity for every nonzero initial vector. The binary determinant and small-noise coefficient follow from an explicit 3x3 lift and simple-eigenvalue perturbation; symbolic identities and finite histories were rerun from the actual standalone verifier. The claim excludes almost-sure growth and a joint small-base-step limit.

The author-hosted 1993 variable-step study addresses deterministic Kepler integration and does not in the inspected material calculate random harmonic-Verlet second moments. The 1992 variable-step obstruction is prior qualitative mathematics, but available abstract only; it does not verify the explicit strict random-law criterion or perturbation coefficient. General positive-map and random-matrix arguments are standard; the claimed specificity is the complete nondegenerate-distribution criterion plus binary exact determinant and universal small-noise coefficient. value.rationale: Random time steps are used to retain symplectic geometry while representing integration uncertainty. The result identifies a universal distinction between pathwise symplectic steps and long-run bounded mean-square energy, with a sharp zero-randomness boundary and a computable positive leading amplification coefficient for practical randomization amplitude choices. Unlike an arbitrary finite slice, it covers every nondegenerate compact step law in the stable interval.
